skill.name: tmux
skill.description: Control tmux sessions for interactive commands, background tasks, service processes, and session cleanup from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.summary: Manage persistent tmux sessions for long-running terminal work and interactive development tasks.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, TypeScript template strings, documented installation paths, and benign shell redirection. The real risk is intentional local command execution through tmux session creation and key sending, plus temporary socket and session metadata storage.

remediation.issue: Caller-provided commands run in local tmux sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly require user confirmation before running untrusted commands, and document that sessions execute with local user permissions.

remediation.issue: Session sockets and metadata are stored in temporary filesystem paths.
remediation.suggestion: Set restrictive permissions on socket and metadata paths and document cleanup expectations for shared machines.

remediation.issue: Documentation references a hidden home-directory install path in many examples.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that this is the skill installation path, not a hidden data store, or prefer a configurable explicit path in examples.

content.value_statement: Long-running terminal tasks are hard to monitor across agent turns. This skill creates, lists, captures, controls, and cleans tmux sessions for persistent command execution.
actual_capabilities: Create named tmux sessions for tasks, services, or agent workflows.
Send keys or commands to an existing tmux pane.
Capture recent pane output for monitoring and debugging.
List session status and metadata stored in a local session file.
Kill individual sessions or clean up old inactive sessions.
Wait for matching text in a tmux pane using helper scripts.
limitations: Requires tmux and the Bun runtime to be installed locally.
Can execute arbitrary user-provided commands inside tmux sessions.
Session metadata and sockets are stored on the local filesystem.
Does not provide remote host isolation or container sandboxing.

use_cases.title: Run long builds outside the main agent turn
use_cases.description: Start a build or test command in tmux, then capture output later without losing process state.

use_cases.title: Manage local development services
use_cases.description: Launch a dev server in a named tmux session and inspect logs while other work continues.

use_cases.title: Drive interactive terminal programs
use_cases.description: Start a REPL or CLI, send input, and capture responses from the same persistent pane.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use for one background command.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tmux skill to start a task named build that runs my project build command. Show me how to capture the latest output.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor a dev server
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate use for a persistent service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tmux service session for my development server, then check whether the server started successfully.

prompt_templates.title: Control an interactive REPL
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use for sending input to a live process.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a Python REPL in tmux, send a simple expression, and capture the response from the pane.

prompt_templates.title: Clean stale sessions safely
prompt_templates.prompt: List all tmux skill sessions, identify inactive sessions older than two days, and clean only those sessions.

output_examples.input: Start a background build and show how I can monitor it.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a named tmux task session and returns the session identifier, attach command, and capture command for later monitoring.

output_examples.input: Check the latest output from my dev server session.
output_examples.output: The skill captures recent pane text and summarizes whether the service appears ready, still starting, or failed.

output: Lists managed sessions with age and status.
Removes sessions older than the requested threshold.
Reports how many sessions were cleaned.

best_practices: Review commands before creating sessions because they run in your local shell context.
Use descriptive session names so cleanup and monitoring are clear.
Capture output before killing a session if logs may be needed later.
anti_patterns: Do not run untrusted commands or paste secrets into managed sessions.
Do not leave long-lived services running without periodic cleanup.
Do not assume tmux sessions isolate commands from your local filesystem.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires tmux, Bun, and a local environment where shell commands may run.

faq.question: Can it run interactive commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can send keys to a tmux pane and capture the pane output later.

faq.question: Does it sandbox commands?
faq.answer: No. Commands run with the same local permissions as the user or agent process.

faq.question: Where are sessions tracked?
faq.answer: The skill stores session metadata and sockets in local temporary or configured filesystem paths.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use it for dev servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can start a server in tmux and inspect output while the agent continues other work.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted input?
faq.answer: No. Treat commands and keystrokes as executable input and review them before use.
